title: Ultralight CMS Architecture Notes
source: Consolidated design commentary from the CW/UltralightCMS project conversations.

points: The original task is to build an ultralight CMS, not a disconnected CW feature showcase.
Every example Node, Property, document and contract exists because the CMS needs it or because it explains the CMS model.
The golden fixture is a normative target for tooling while it remains unlocked.
Entity and Property are the only canonical atoms.
A Node is an interpreted Entity; every Node is therefore an abstraction.
ABS is the least opinionated standard family; other families are predefined abstraction contracts.
Properties carry semantics. Function, Event, Effect, Data, Schema, Asset, Members, Required Link and Link are Properties.
One truth. Many topologies. No duplicate truth.
FILE is the primary implementation family in this fixture.
DOC provides semantic document scope through members; its Asset is presentation/explanation payload only.
CTRCT owns reusable CMS contracts such as schemas; implementation FILE Nodes reference those contracts rather than duplicating them.
NodeType reads choose default projection surfaces and never whitelist all valid Properties.
The same canonical Entity may belong to multiple abstractions through members without cloning identity.
Format defines how the package is interpreted.
Model contains canonical semantic truth and the authoritative shard manifest.
Assets contain physical payloads owned by Entities and remain opaque to the CW package validator.
.cw is the canonical model artifact extension and .cwn is the package-local NodeType template extension.
Filesystem topology derives from identities and physical package structure.
Dependency topology derives from dependency Link Properties.
Runtime causal topology derives from Event, Function, Effect and their Link Properties.
Abstraction/document scope derives from members Properties.
A topology is projected from the canonical model; it is not stored as a second graph truth.
